Dropped: TTS (->voice-tts), translation/dubbing (->translation), summarization/meeting-notes, agentwonderland business, YouTube-transcript scrapers, orbisapi voice-analysis, x402 Helper demos. dTelecom 'STT' dropped — indexed URLs were /favicon.ico, root, /docs.md (not callable endpoints). resolved = agentcash exact prices.

entries.name: OpenAI Whisper
entries.description: OpenAI speech-to-text — Whisper (incl. large-v3) and gpt-4o-transcribe. Multi-format audio, language detection, srt/vtt output.

usage.outputShape: body.result (EMPTY {} in test — no transcript returned); body.success=true, body.meta.upstreamPaid=true but no usable text
quirks: Paid $0.009, returned HTTP 200 with success:true and meta.upstreamPaid:true, but body.result was an EMPTY object {} — no transcript text delivered.
Charge-then-empty: it takes payment and claims upstream success but returns no usable transcription.
Has an aggressive shared rate limit: 'Maximum 15 requests per 15 minutes' (error mentions 'report generation', suggesting a shared generic proxy backend), returns 429 with retryAfter:900.
Field name audio_url is accepted (no 4xx) but did not yield output; 'url'+'model' attempt was rate-limited before it could be evaluated.
Pays on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; price $0.0090.
usage.guide: Do not rely on this endpoint for transcription. In testing a paid call (POST with {audio_url: <public mp3>}) returned HTTP 200 and success:true with meta.upstreamPaid:true, but body.result came back as an empty object {} with no transcript text — money charged ($0.009), no usable output. A second attempt with a different body field was blocked by a strict shared rate limit (15 requests / 15 minutes, 429 with retryAfter:900). Treat as broken; if re-checking later, send {audio_url} pointing at a small public audio file and verify body.result actually contains transcript text before trusting it.

entries.name: ElevenLabs Scribe
entries.description: ElevenLabs Scribe — audio-to-text with speaker diarization, word/character timestamps, and audio-event tagging.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/elevenlabs/v1/speech-to-text with multipart/form-data fields: model_id=scribe_v1 + file=<audio binary> (NOT JSON)
usage.outputShape: unknown — never received a 2xx (server rejected JSON body before transcription)
quirks: Endpoint is a multipart/form-data proxy to ElevenLabs Scribe, NOT a JSON endpoint.
Required field model_id (e.g. scribe_v1) plus the audio in a multipart 'file' field (100ms minimum audio).
A JSON request body is ignored entirely: the server's validator reports input:null and 422 'model_id field required' even when model_id IS present in the JSON.
source_url / cloud_storage_url are documented in the registry inputSchema but were NOT honored when sent in a JSON body (same 422).
The money-safe JSON x402 pay primitive (qa-pay) cannot call this endpoint — it hard-codes Content-Type: application/json and JSON-stringifies the body, so it cannot build multipart with a file part.

x402 charges $0.030 USDC on Base BEFORE the multipart validation runs, so a JSON call pays then 422s with no refund (lost $0.03 in this test, tx 0xddab6aeb849c909426d2dc0e1e83ace7d3851e04d57c24ec53d8746971c5ce31).
usage.guide: Call POST https://x402.orth.sh/elevenlabs/v1/speech-to-text as multipart/form-data, not JSON. Send form field model_id=scribe_v1 and the audio as the file form field (at least 100ms of audio); optional fields: diarize, language_code, tag_audio_events, num_speakers, timestamps_granularity. Pay the $0.030 x402 USDC charge on Base. Do NOT send a JSON body — the server ignores it and returns 422 after charging you. A JSON-only x402 client (like the qa-pay primitive) cannot use this endpoint; you need a client that can build multipart bodies with the x402 payment header attached.

usage.callShape: POST https://cnvrt.ing/api/transcribe with JSON body {url, includeTimestamps?, language?, enhanceAccuracy?}
usage.outputShape: body.transcription (string), body.success, body.jobId, body.language, body.duration, body.wordCount, body.timestamps[]{start,end,text} (when includeTimestamps:true)
quirks: Host cnvrt.ing is unreachable as of 2026-06-08: DNS does not resolve (connection timed out, no servers reachable) and HTTP returns 000 after a 15-30s timeout.
Control host google.com returned HTTP 200 in 0.2s from the same sandbox, confirming the network is fine and the failure is host-side.
qa-pay returned classification 'wallet-error' / 'provider request failed: fetch failed' with paid:false on two attempts — no USDC was spent because the connection never established.
Earlier probe (2026-06-01) showed a 402 (payable); the service has since gone offline.
usage.guide: This endpoint is currently dead. As of 2026-06-08 cnvrt.ing does not resolve via DNS and all requests time out (HTTP 000), confirmed against a working control host. When live, the documented call is POST https://cnvrt.ing/api/transcribe with JSON body {"url":"<media URL>"} (optional includeTimestamps, language ISO-639-1, enhanceAccuracy), paid via x402, and the result text would be at body.transcription with metadata at body.duration/wordCount and timestamp segments at body.timestamps[]. Do not call until reachability is re-confirmed.

usage.callShape: POST https://convert.kasandell.workers.dev/convert/audio with a RAW BINARY audio body (the audio file bytes themselves, NOT JSON), Content-Type: audio/mpeg (or matching the file format). Pay via x402 (USDC on Base, eip155:8453, $0.003).

inputExample._note: Body is NOT JSON. Send raw audio file bytes (e.g. an MP3) as the POST body with Content-Type: audio/mpeg. Supported: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC, WebM.

quirks: Body must be RAW BINARY audio bytes, NOT JSON. Empty inputSchema in registry is misleading — the real input is the audio file itself in the request body.
Content-Type must be audio/* (decoded payment-required bazaar extension specifies audio/mpeg, bodyType=binary). Supported formats: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC, WebM.

COULD NOT VERIFY via the money-safe qa-pay tool: that tool reads --body=@file as UTF-8 text and forwards a string to wallet.paidFetch, which irreversibly corrupts binary audio. A pay primitive with binary-body support is required to test this endpoint.
Endpoint appears live and well-formed: probe returns 402 with valid x402 accepts (USDC/Base, payTo 0x043b8aa7e75068F92696c8831801587Fc105A8d8, amount 3000 = $0.003) and a clear {text} output schema.
usage.guide: Transcribe audio to text. POST the raw bytes of an audio file (MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC, or WebM) directly as the request body to https://convert.kasandell.workers.dev/convert/audio with Content-Type set to the audio type (e.g. audio/mpeg) — do NOT wrap it in JSON. Pay $0.003 USDC on Base via x402. The response is JSON; read the transcription from body.text. NOTE: this was not paid-verified because the QA pay tool cannot transmit a binary body without UTF-8 corruption.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.hookfindr.com/api/x402/transcribe with JSON body {"url":"<public short-form video URL>"}
usage.outputShape: body.text (full transcript string); body.words[] (array of {word, start, end} timestamps in seconds); body.word_count; body.transcript_source (e.g. "whisper_v3_turbo"); body.duration_s; body.source/body.cached (cache flags); body.music and body.summary may be null
quirks: MUST send the video URL in a JSON POST body as {"url":"..."} — the bazaar payment-required header advertises input as type:http with queryParams:{url}, but passing ?url=... as a query param returns HTTP 400 {"error":"invalid json"} AND STILL CHARGES (lost $0.05 on the query-param attempt).
Input is a PUBLIC short-form VIDEO URL (TikTok/YouTube/Shorts/Instagram Reels/Twitter-X/Twitch/Facebook, ~1000 platforms via yt-dlp), NOT an audio file URL.
Uses native platform captions when available (~2s) and falls back to Whisper-large-v3-turbo on extracted audio (~30s); known songs return LRCLIB synced lyrics instead.
Responses are cached: re-calling the same video URL returns source:"cache", cached:true (you still pay $0.05 per call).
usage.guide: POST to https://api.hookfindr.com/api/x402/transcribe with a JSON body {"url":"<public video URL>"} (Content-Type application/json) and pay the $0.05 x402 charge on Base. Do NOT pass the URL as a query parameter — that returns 400 invalid json yet still charges you. The url must be a public short-form video link (TikTok, YouTube, Shorts, Instagram Reels, X, Twitch, Facebook, etc.). Read the transcript from body.text and per-word timestamps from body.words[] ({word,start,end} in seconds); transcript_source tells you whether native captions or Whisper was used. Synchronous — the full result is in the paid response, no polling.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402-ai-api.civicmerge.workers.dev/v1/audio/transcribe with JSON body {file: <audio>} (x402 USDC on Base, $0.020). NOTE: backend 500s on every JSON encoding tried.
usage.outputShape: Declared output: body.text (e.g. {"text":"Hello, world."}). NOT OBSERVED — server returned 500 plain-text "Internal Server Error" instead.
quirks: Backend is broken: pays then returns HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' (text/plain). Charge-then-fail — payment settles but no transcription is returned.

inputSchema says 'file' is multipart form-data binary, but the live bazaar metadata declares bodyType=json with body {file: '<binary audio data>'} and output example {text: 'Hello, world.'} — contradictory.
Tried file as raw base64 string AND as data:audio/wav;base64 data-URL in a JSON body; both 500'd.

Untested: true multipart/form-data file upload (qa-pay only sends application/json, so the multipart path could not be exercised). The 500 may be specific to JSON; a multipart client might behave differently but was not verifiable here.
Spent $0.04 total across 2 paid attempts, both 500.
usage.guide: This speech-to-text endpoint is currently broken via JSON: it accepts the x402 payment ($0.020 USDC on Base) and then returns HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' with no transcription. Two JSON encodings of the audio (raw base64 and base64 data-URL in a {file:...} body) were paid for and both 500'd. The declared success shape is {"text": "..."} read from body.text, but it was never observed. A fresh agent should treat this as broken; if attempting, the only untried path is a real multipart/form-data file upload (the schema's stated format), but expect to lose money given the consistent 500s.
